messages:
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout v3.8.1 -> region-us-west (10% traffic). healthchecks green initially, stepping to 30% now.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: CANARY_5XX_SPIKE fired (service: inference-canary). triggered at 1766005432. priority: P1.
maria: acked pager (maria) — I'm on it, switching to #incidents. grabbing context.
jamie: saw a small 5xx uptick on tail-sampling, p95 tokens spiked too. rolling metrics: `embed-service` upstream 502s.
sre-oncall: can folks paste the canary config? did we change kv-proxy or tokenization logic in this rollout?
kevin: no kv-proxy changes in this patch — main diffs were decoder kernel and batching heuristics.
carol: live dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/infer/canary - error rate jumped from 0.2% -> 4.8% right at traffic shift to 30%.
ops-runner: running quick check: `kubectl get pods -l app=inference-canary -n prod -o wide` — pods are CrashLooping on a subset (oom/killed).
jamie: can we isolate which model variant? looks like quantized-x64 was used for canary. fallback path maybe hitting a kernel path.
incident-bot: escalation: 2nd line notified (sre-oncall rotation). PD: escalating to on-call if unacked in 2m.
maria: tagging @kevin @jamie @carol — propose immediate traffic divert back to stable and pause rollout. I can flip the route.
kevin: agree. I'll initiate traffic diversion. hold on.
kevin: executing: ```
kubectl annotate svc/inference-route traffic-percent-stable=100 --overwrite
redwoodctl route set canary --weight 0 --namespace=prod
```
ops-runner: logs from a failing pod: ```
E0301 12:10:27.123 inference.c:512] kv-cache: failed open mmap: Input/output error
ERROR: decoder kernel failed: unaligned read at 0x7fbf...\n```
jamie: that looks like a kernel-level segfault for quant path. might be a mismatch between kernel and compiled model artifact.
carol: customer impact: we have ~12 requests/min failing, mostly non-streaming embed calls from EU region. escalating to support.
pd-bot: PagerDuty note: on-call acknowledged by maria at 1766005450. escalation timer paused.
sre-oncall: while traffic is diverting, please snapshot canary pods and keep them alive for postmortem. don't delete yet.
maria: traffic now 100% stable. error rate dropped back to baseline. confirming with graphs. :thumbsup:
kevin: snapshot done: `kubectl cp pod/inference-canary-1:/var/log/infer/logs ./snapshots/canary-1766005432/`
ops-runner: creating short-lived rollback plan — we should roll the canary image back to v3.7.9 and re-run CI kernel-compat checks.
jamie: agreed. plan: 1) pause rollout (done), 2) divert traffic (done), 3) rollback canary image, 4) run hybrid warmup on a small fraction with extra telemetry, 5) re-promote if stable.
kevin: performing `redwoodctl rollout set inference-canary --image=registry/redwood/infer:3.7.9 --namespace=prod` now.
ops-runner: command output: ```
rollout: update started -> rolling update 3/3 pods
waiting for readiness...
```
carol: pinging support to notify affected customers — minimal impact but want transparency. support ticket opened: #SUP-11456.
maria: PD: I'm staying on the thread until rollback verified. anyone else stepping off?
kevin: pods are back to Ready on 3.7.9, p95 latency and error rate trending to baseline.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: CANARY_5XX_SPIKE resolved at 1766005720 (ack by maria).
jamie: running quick post-rollback smoke: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/embed -d '{"text":"probe"}'` -> 200 OK.
sre-oncall: leaving a note to add kernel compatibility test to canary gating. ticket: INF-2392.
maria: thanks everyone — I'll file a short incident write-up and loop in eng-ml for artifact-build checks. we avoided broad customer impact, no rollback to prod needed.
kevin: small follow-up: we should add a safety flag to prevent quantized kernels from being scheduled to canary until we have a matched runtime.
carol: copying in product & support for awareness. :email:
pd-bot: PagerDuty: incident closed by maria.
ops-runner: saving thread logs & artifacts to: s3://redwood-incidents/1766005432/
maria: great job—handing off to postmortem runway. will assign owners and ETA for write-up. :white_check_mark:
